summary: Calculates days in force and pro-rated earned premium per policy for calendar years 2021 through 2025 based on policy active date overlaps.
risk_notes: DATEDIFF and inclusive bounds: T-SQL DATEDIFF(DAY, ...) combined with '+ 1' calculates inclusive days in range; PySpark datediff(end, start) counts boundaries and requires precise +1 handling to avoid off-by-one errors.

Hardcoded 365 divisor: The formula uses a fixed 365.0 denominator, ignoring leap years like 2024 (which has 366 days); PySpark implementations must preserve this explicit rule rather than using actual year day-counts.
Hardcoded year range: The inline VALUES (2021)..(2025) table limits the output scope and will omit earned premium for policies active in 2026+ unless dynamically generated in Spark.

Rounding semantics: SQL Server ROUND() behaves as half-away-from-zero for numeric types, whereas PySpark round() defaults to HALF_UP and bround() to HALF_EVEN, potentially causing penny-rounding discrepancies.

NULL date handling: IIF with NULL start_date or end_date evaluates to NULL in T-SQL, resulting in NULL days_in_force; PySpark date functions must ensure identical null-propagation behavior without throwing runtime exceptions.
